FLUORESCENCE IN SITU HYBRIDIZATION (FISH) REPORT

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient: [redacted name]
Age/Sex: 33-year-old male
MRN: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Lymph node biopsy
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL DETAILS
Clinical Indication: Lymph node biopsy tissue section analysis
Suspected Diagnosis: Follicular lymphoma

TEST PERFORMED
Interphase FISH Analysis for IGH/BCL2 Rearrangement

METHODOLOGY
Interphase FISH analysis was performed on formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue sections using the Vysis LSI IGH/BCL2 Dual Color, Dual Fusion Translocation Probe (Abbott Molecular). The analysis was correlated with CD79a immunostained slides to identify B-cell populations. Both intrafollicular and interfollicular regions were evaluated separately.

Probe Information:
- IGH probe (14q32): SpectrumGreen
- BCL2 probe (18q21): SpectrumOrange
- Expected normal pattern: 2 green, 2 orange signals
- Expected abnormal pattern (with t(14;18)): 1 green, 1 orange, 2 fusion signals

RESULTS

IGH/BCL2 [t(14;18)] Rearrangement Analysis:

Intrafollicular regions:
- Cells analyzed: 200
- Normal signal pattern (2G2O): 198/200 (99%)
- Abnormal signal pattern: 2/200 (1%)
- Result: NEGATIVE for IGH/BCL2 rearrangement

Interfollicular regions:
- Cells analyzed: 200
- Normal signal pattern (2G2O): 197/200 (98.5%)
- Abnormal signal pattern: 3/200 (1.5%)
- Result: NEGATIVE for IGH/BCL2 rearrangement

Overall Result: No evidence of IGH/BCL2 [t(14;18)] rearrangement detected

INTERPRETATION
FISH analysis shows no evidence of the IGH/BCL2 translocation t(14;18) in either the intrafollicular or interfollicular regions of this lymph node biopsy. The t(14;18) translocation is typically associated with 85-90% of follicular lymphomas and results in BCL2 overexpression. The absence of this translocation in the context of suspected follicular lymphoma may suggest:

1. A BCL2-negative follicular lymphoma (10-15% of cases)
2. An alternative B-cell lymphoma diagnosis
3. A reactive lymphoid process

Correlation with morphology, immunophenotyping, and clinical findings is recommended for definitive diagnosis.

AUTHORIZED BY:
[redacted name], M.D.
Director, Molecular Cytogenetics Laboratory
[redacted location] Medical Center
